description: Prioritization + ranking algorithms — how to order a backlog, a work queue, or a candidate set by value/urgency/cost. A registry of algorithm SPECS (what it computes, its inputs, when to use it, whether it is deterministic), not implementations; pointers, never truth. Composes with queueing_disciplines (the serving order), triage_algorithms (the routing decision), decision_policy (thresholds), and formulas (the scoring math). Deterministic-first: prefer a transparent scoring rule over a learned ranker until the lift is proven.

algorithms.name: Weighted scoring
algorithms.when_to_use: transparent, explainable priority with a few agreed factors

algorithms.name: Weighted Shortest Job First
algorithms.when_to_use: maximize economic value delivered per unit effort on a backlog

algorithms.name: RICE
algorithms.when_to_use: product backlog prioritization with rough estimates

algorithms.name: MCDA / TOPSIS
algorithms.what: rank by closeness to the ideal solution across weighted criteria
algorithms.when_to_use: many competing criteria, some conflicting; needs a defensible multi-criteria order

algorithms.name: Eisenhower (urgent/important)
algorithms.when_to_use: fast triage of a personal/ops task list

algorithms.name: Learning-to-rank (LTR)
algorithms.what: a model scores items from labeled relevance/outcomes
algorithms.when_to_use: high-volume ranking where a transparent rule under-performs AND you have outcome labels; admit only on proven lift (two-axis gate)
